title: Integer multiplicity slice boundaries of a cycle with the integer slice property
statement:
Assume (SL), the exact frozen statement of the DAG theorem cmc_slice_mass_bounds, which appears verbatim (parenthesized) as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement. (SL) says: let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), and let μ, μ' be measures finite on compact subsets of U. Let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{k+1}(ℝ^P) and ξ' : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) be a.e. strongly measurable (for μ, resp. μ') with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ-a.e. and |ξ'(x)(α)| ≤ |α| μ'-a.e., with T(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ and ∂T(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms on U. Then for every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ there are A_t ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (t ∈ ℝ) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ'. Moreover ∂A_t(η) = B_t(η) whenever tsupport η is disjoint from {f = t}, and for open W, M_W(∂A_t − B_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h↓0}h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h < f < t}) and ∫_a^b M_W(∂A_t − B_t)dt ≤ Lμ(W ∩ {a < f < b}).
Now let P, d ∈ ℕ and X ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with ∂X = 0. Let μX be a measure on ℝ^P with μX(K) < ∞ for every compact K. Let ξX : ℝ^P → Λ_{d+1}(ℝ^P) be μX-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξX(x)(α)| ≤ |α| (|α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α) for μX-a.e. x and every α, and with X(ω) = ∫ξX(x)(ω(x))dμX(x) for every test (d+1)-form ω on ℝ^P. Suppose X has the integer slice property ISP (hypothesis copied verbatim from the parent statement): for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of X and (μ', ξ') of ∂X (measures finite on compact sets; a.e. strongly measurable fields bounded by |α| a.e.; representing X, resp. ∂X, on all test forms) and every L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t, all A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms have ∂A − B integer multiplicity. Then for every L ≥ 0 and every L-Lipschitz g : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ there is A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{{x : g(x) < t}} ξX(x)(ω(x)) dμX(x) for every test (d+1)-form ω, and with ∂A integer multiplicity.
